data.name: Ravindrasinh
data.long_meaning: Ravindra means 'Lord of the Sun' and Sinh means 'Lion'. Thus, Ravindrasinh means 'Lord of the Sun, Lion-borne'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ravindrasinh is a powerful name that signifies strength, courage, and the power of the sun. It is a name that is often given to babies who are expected to lead and inspire others.
data.numerology_meaning: Ravindrasinh is a name that resonates with creativity, self-expression, and communication. It suggests a life path of artistic or communicative pursuits, and a deep connection to the emotional and spiritual aspects of life.

in_sanskrit.name: रविन्द्रसिंह
in_sanskrit.meaning: रवि (Ravi) - One who delights in the sight of Lord Vishnu, दन्द (Sinh) - Lion, सिंह (Sinh) - A name given to a king or a ruler
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: One who delights in the sight of Lord Vishnu (Ravi) and is a lion (Sinh) or a king.

in_hindi.name: रविन्द्रसिंह
in_hindi.meaning: रवि (Ravi) - विष्वक्सेन (Vishnu) का अनुभवी, सिंह (Sinh) - सिंह (Lion) या राजा (King)
in_hindi.long_meaning: One who embodies the experiences of Lord Vishnu (Ravi) and is a lion (Sinh) or a king.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ravindrasinh" has rich cultural significance in Hinduism. The Hindu pantheon includes the mighty sun-god, Surya, who is often depicted as a lion. Ravindrasinh, with the name signifying a connection to both the sun and the lion, symbolizes strength, courage, and the radiant power of the sun deity.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Ravindrasinh represents the power and might of the divine sun, which brings life and light to the world. This name also highlights the inner strength, courage, and fierce determination of an individual. The spiritual significance of the name can serve as a reminder that, like the sun, individuals have the power to bring light, warmth, and growth to those around them.

historical_references.reference: Ravindrasinh was a Jain monk and a poet in medieval India. He is known for his work, the 'Kautūlya Prabandha', which was written in 1336 CE.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Jain monk and poet

historical_references.reference: Ravindrasinh was a Maratha general and a poet who served under the Peshwa (Maratha ruler) Baji Rao I during the late 17th and early 18th centuries. He is known for his 'Abhijañanā' work, which is a Marathi commentary on the Sanskrit text 'Aṣṭādhyayī'.
